correctness.rationale: The proof gives an explicit common subcomplex U, decomposes its star factors and their integral circle homology, then specifies actual relative elementary collapses D searrow U and L searrow U. The first collapses require at least two second-level children so each b-cone has an outside leaf; the second require each leaf set nonempty. The composition U -> L -> D proves that the actual inclusion L -> D is a homotopy equivalence. The simplicial mapping cone then makes K contractible. Join of M connected wedges of circles yields B spheres in dimension 2M-1 with free integral homology. Fully enumerated binary and nonuniform examples verify face counts, actual free pairs and GF(2) ranks; infinite correctness rests on the proof, not enumeration.

originality.rationale: The strongest directly pertinent older theorem covers perfect regular trees, including ambient contractibility in the uniform subfamily, and the published height-two result covers punctured branch factors. Neither includes the irregular height-three root-link homotopy equivalence, a statement about an actual inclusion map, nor is there a stronger coverage result found in the inspected primary sources or published-finding corpus searches. These overlapping components are credited explicitly. Unindexed equivalences remain a genuine residual priority risk.

value.rationale: The contrast between contractible ambient complexes and exponentially many primitive homology classes exposed by deletion of a single root is a natural local stability invariant of graph independence topology. The theorem gives the full arbitrary nonuniform family, the precise integral rank and dimension, and a stronger homotopy equivalence for the actual link inclusion. This structural map cannot be inferred from ambient Betti numbers and can be reused in link-deletion and robustness arguments. The regular ambient subcase is credited, not presented as new.
